title: TEAD Palmitoylation Inhibitors are Brain Penetrant and Enhance Survival in Preclinical Models of Recurrent Glioblastoma in Combination with Standard-of-Care Therapy
summary: Abstract Purpose: Oncogenic addiction to YAP-TEAD signaling drives adaptive plasticity, therapeutic resistance, invasion and tumor progression in many cancers, including in glioblastoma (GBM), and represents an actionable vulnerability to explore as adjuvant therapy during tumor recurrence. This study evaluated the translational potential of orally bioavailable Vivace Therapeutics (VT) TEAD palmitoylation inhibitors in preclinical GBM models. Experimental Design: The effects of VT103 and VT104 on GBM proliferation, migration, and TEAD activity were first assessed across patient-derived GBM cell lines with diverse genomic drivers. The drugs pharmacokinetics (PK) and biodistribution were measured using mass spectrometry in mice bearing patient-derived orthotopic xenograft (PDX) GBM. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in two genetically distinct PDX models of recurrent GBM, administering VT104 as monotherapy or in combination with standard-of-care radiotherapy plus temozolomide (RT+TMZ). Results: VT104/VT103 treatment significantly impaired GBM proliferation and migration in-vitro, with concomitant downregulation of TEAD-target expression. PK studies confirmed sustained VT104 plasma levels and robust brain biodistribution in PDX mice, with brain:plasma ratio >150% at therapeutic dosing without systemic toxicity. While VT104 monotherapy showed modest anti-tumor effects, combination therapy (VT104+RT+TMZ) significantly extended overall survival in both recurrent GBM PDX models. The survival benefit was most prominent in EGFR-mutant GBM and corresponded to significant decrease in overall and infiltrative tumor burden. Mechanistically, VT104 potentiated TMZ-dependent {gamma}-H2AX genotoxic stress and RT+TMZ synergized with VT104 to abolish TEAD activity. Conclusion: Integrating YAP-TEAD inhibition with standard therapy introduces a clinically-relevant paradigm for synergistic treatment in recurrent GBM that both inhibits tumor infiltration and reduces therapeutic resistanc

title: Spatial organization of a SPINK1-associated tumor-stromal ecosystem links metabolic remodeling to immune restriction in bladder cancer
summary: Spatially organized tumor-stromal interactions contribute to metabolic remodeling and immune suppression in bladder cancer (BLCA). Using spatial transcriptional programs to define single-cell states, we identified a niche comprising SPINK1-high epithelial cells (E2) and TPM2-high cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) (C1). SPINK1 promoted tumor growth and myofibroblastic CAF programs, with EGFR and TGF-{beta} signaling implicated in tumor-CAF communication. Inferred metabolic reactions and spatial metabolite distributions supported a candidate circuit linking tumor-derived lactate to CAF oxidative metabolism and glutamine provision, followed by tumor glutamine utilization for reductive carboxylation and fatty acid synthesis. SPINK1 perturbation altered extracellular glutamine and lactate concentrations. Predicted chemokine interactions implicated C2/C3 CAFs in T cell recruitment, whereas the E2-C1 niche exhibited checkpoint and exhaustion-associated features. RHCG-positive tumor regions contained higher proportions of TOXCXCR4 cells among CD3 T cells, suggesting a possible association between ammonia handling and T cell dysfunction. In vivo, Spink1 loss attenuated tumor progression, increased cytotoxic CD8 T-cell infiltration, and enhanced tumor control during PD-1 blockade. These findings identify a spatially organized tumor-stromal niche associated with metabolic cooperation and immune restriction, supporting SPINK1 as a candidate therapeutic target in combination with immunotherapy.

title: Metastatic G2 laryngeal neuroendocrine tumor treated with sulfatinib and sintilimab: A case report and literature review.
authors: Luo Y, Mao A, Li X et al.
abstract:
RATIONALE: Laryngeal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are rare and heterogeneous malignancies with limited evidence guiding the management of metastatic disease. We report a metastatic G2 laryngeal NET initially presenting as an unusual temporal subcutaneous metastasis and subsequently treated with combined targeted therapy and immunotherapy.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 63-year-old man with a history of invasive lung adenocarcinoma presented with a 1.3 × 1.2 cm left temporal subcutaneous nodule and a history of hoarseness accompanied by throat pain.
DIAGNOSES: Histopathological examination of the temporal lesion suggested metastatic NET. Subsequent PET-CT, laryngoscopy, and biopsy identified a primary laryngeal NET. After vertical partial laryngectomy, right neck dissection, and laryngeal function reconstruction, pathology confirmed a well-differentiated G2 NET with cervical lymph-node and temporal subcutaneous metastases, classified as pT2N1M1, stage IVC. In March 2025, hepatic metastases were pathologically confirmed. Molecular profiling identified HRAS p.Q61L, KDR p.S265L, and ROS1 p.S615Y variants, microsatellite instability-high status, and programmed death-ligand 1expression with a combined positive score of 70.
INTERVENTIONS: Combination therapy with sulfatinib (300 mg/day) and sintilimab (200 mg every 3 weeks) was initiated in April 2025 and continued without dose reduction, interruption, or delay.
OUTCOMES: After 10 months of combination therapy, contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a reduction in the size of hepatic metastatic lesions compared with baseline, together with a marked decrease in the number of metastatic lesions. The largest index hepatic lesion decreased from 32.68 mm to 19.05 mm in maximal diameter, corresponding to a 41.7% reduction, demonstrating a marked radiological reduction in hepatic metastatic burden. At the latest documented assessment in February 2026, no further disease progression or treatment-related adverse events were observed.
LESSONS: This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of metastatic laryngeal NET with an unusual subcutaneous presentation. Comprehensive pathological and molecular evaluation may aid treatment decision-making in advanced disease. The observed disease control with sulfatinib plus sintilimab is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in additional patients.

title: Navitoclax overcomes epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated resistance in ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer with rapid disease progression during alectinib treatment.
authors: Nishimura T, Tomida S, Kuribayashi T et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) generally responds to the ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) alectinib; however, some patients experience rapid disease progression shortly after treatment initiation. This study investigated the molecular features underlying this clinically distinct phenotype and evaluated potential therapeutic strategies using patient-derived models.
METHODS: A 68-year-old woman with ALK-positive NSCLC experienced disease progression within 1 month of first-line alectinib therapy despite an initial transient tumor response. Two resistant cell lines were established from an adrenal metastasis and a pleural effusion, respectively. Histopathological and molecular characterization was performed. The combination of ALK-TKIs and the B-cell lymphoma 2 family inhibitor navitoclax was evaluated in vitro and in vivo.
RESULTS: Both cell lines harbored the EML4-ALK fusion variant 1 without secondary ALK mutations and demonstrated resistance to multiple ALK-TKIs. Transcriptomic profiling demonstrated epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated features in the resistant cell lines, supported by concordant immunohistochemical findings in the pretreatment specimen. Melanoma-associated antigen 3 (MAGE-A3) was identified as the most highly upregulated gene, and its knockdown significantly enhanced ALK-TKI sensitivity. Navitoclax combined with ALK-TKIs synergistically reduced cell viability and enhanced apoptosis in vitro, and lorlatinib plus navitoclax produced greater antitumor efficacy than either monotherapy in vivo.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that pre-existing EMT-associated features, together with MAGE-A3 upregulation and impaired apoptotic signaling, may contribute to rapid disease progression during alectinib treatment in a subset of ALK-positive NSCLC patients. Targeting apoptotic vulnerability with navitoclax in combination with ALK-TKIs warrants further investigation as a therapeutic strategy for this resistance phenotype.

title: PM54 induces transcriptional collapse across cell-derived and patient-derived cancer models.
authors: Diez MM, Fernández-Miranda I, Nuñez GS et al.
abstract: Oncogenic transcriptional programs sustain malignant cell states and create therapeutic vulnerabilities in cancer. Here, we evaluated the antitumor activity and mechanism of PM54, a next-generation synthetic ecteinascidin analog, across diverse preclinical models. PM54 was tested in a 59-cell-line panel, mechanistic flow cytometry assays, short-term RNA sequencing in 32 cancer cell lines, six cell-derived xenografts (CDX), and three patient-derived orthotopic xenografts (PDOX). PM54 formed stable DNA adducts and showed broad low-nanomolar antiproliferative activity, with a mean half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 4.19 nM. Mechanistically, PM54 reduced nascent RNA synthesis, decreased RNA polymerase II levels, activated DNA-damage signaling, promoted S-phase accumulation, and triggered apoptosis. Short-term RNA sequencing revealed conserved repression of cell cycle, DNA repair, MYC-, mTOR-, and RNA polymerase II-associated programs. Pathway-level analyses identified two transcriptional response patterns, termed primed and adaptive patterns, differing in the extent of PM54-induced suppression of proliferative and oncogenic pathways. In vivo, PM54 reduced tumor growth and extended survival across six CDX models, with complete regressions in selected small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), melanoma, and prostate cancer models. In three PDOX models, PM54 reduced tumor burden by 81% in an experimentally generated cisplatin-resistant high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, 69% in ovarian clear cell carcinoma, and 84% in gastric adenocarcinoma. These findings support evaluation of PM54 as a transcription-targeting therapeutic.

title: Research Trends in Artificial Intelligence Applications in Dental Hygiene and Dentistry in Korean Academic Journals: A Scoping Review.
authors: Jung EH, Kim BR, Jeong SJ et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This scoping review examined research on artificial intelligence (AI) published in Korean academic journals in the fields of dental hygiene and dentistry. The Context-Concept-Maturity framework was applied to compare research trends and identify future directions.
METHODS: Following the Arksey and O'Malley framework, with extensions by Levac et al., the review adhered to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Domestic academic journals published between January 1, 2020, and September 30, 2025, were searched in KISS, RISS, ScienceON, and DBpia. Studies were screened, extracted, and coded according to population, concept, and context criteria, yielding 70 eligible articles (26 in dental hygiene and 44 in dentistry).
RESULTS: In dental hygiene, most research focused on education (38.5%) and community/public oral health (38.5%), while clinical applications were limited (7.7%). Major conceptual domains included education/training tools (42.3%), workflow/automation (38.5%), prediction (15.4%), and classification (3.8%). Dentistry studies were predominantly clinically oriented and imaging-based, emphasizing classification, automation, and segmentation. Maturity analysis indicated that dentistry primarily occupied Stage 2 (application; ∼84.1%), whereas dental hygiene showed a dual distribution across Stage 1 (exploration; 46.2%) and Stage 2 (application; 46.2%), with limited Stage 3 (integration; 7.7%) studies.
CONCLUSION: AI research in Korea exhibits divergent developmental trajectories. Dental hygiene research emphasizes education, prevention, and public oral health, combining exploratory and applied approaches, while dentistry demonstrates greater clinical integration and application-level maturity. Advancing AI maturity in dental hygiene will require expansion of clinical data-driven studies, incorporation of AI and data literacy into curricula, standardized integration of unstructured and clinical data, multicenter long-term validation, and the development of ethical and performance governance frameworks.

title: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis.
authors: Tateishi M, Otsuka Y, Matsuoka R et al.
abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE subtypes; however, an ambiguous state is observed for some specimens, which shows the simultaneous expression of NE and non-NE lineage markers. The findings of this study indicate that LCNEC may transit toward the NE or non-NE directions. By controlling the transcriptional regulatory networks of such elasticity, a new approach may be contemplated to overcome the pleiotropic therapeutic responses of LCNEC.

title: First-in-human, phase I study of clesitamig, a DLL3-targeted CD3×4-1BB trispecific T-cell engager in patients with advanced small-cell lung cancer and other neuroendocrine carcinomas.
authors: Yoshida T, Fowler S, Franjkovic I et al.

title: T-cell engagers in small-cell lung cancer: from development to safety management of a breakthrough immunotherapy strategy for solid tumors.
authors: Peroni M, Di Odoardo A, Andrini E et al.
abstract: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a highly aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy characterized by rapid progression, early metastatic spread, and limited efficacy of treatment options beyond first-line chemo-immunotherapy. T-cell engagers (TCEs) have emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy, redirecting cytotoxic T cells toward tumor-associated antigens independently of pre-existing antitumor immunity. Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3), expressed in approximately 85-90% of SCLC tumors and minimally in normal tissues, represents an attractive therapeutic target. Tarlatamab, the first-in-class DLL3-directed bispecific T-cell engager, has demonstrated clinically meaningful antitumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with SCLC, including durable responses and signals of intracranial efficacy. Its safety profile reflects its mechanism of action and is primarily driven by T-cell activation and cytokine release. Treatment-emergent adverse events mainly include cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). CRS is common but predominantly low grade (grade 1-2), with early onset and rapid resolution following supportive management, including intravenous fluids, oxygen, vasopressors, and IL-6 antagonists such as tocilizumab when clinically indicated. ICANS occurs less frequently, typically presents later, and is also mostly low grade with slower resolution. Both toxicities are generally manageable in appropriately trained clinical settings. Several additional DLL3-targeted TCEs and combination strategies are under investigation, showing encouraging preliminary efficacy and improved safety profiles. Ongoing efforts focus on optimizing outpatient administration, mitigating toxicity, and refining patient selection through biomarker development. This review summarizes the biological rationale, preclinical and clinical development, safety management, and emerging clinical evidence supporting the role of TCEs in SCLC.

title: Pembrolizumab After Radiation Therapy and Chemotherapy in Limited Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer
conditions: Limited Stage Lung Small Cell Carcinoma
summary: This phase II trial studies how well pembrolizumab after standard treatment with radiation plus the following chemotherapy drugs: cisplatin or carboplatin, plus etoposide works in treating patients with limited stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC). Immunotherapy with monoclonal antibodies, such as pembrolizumab, may help the body's immune system attack the cancer, and may interfere with the ability of tumor cells to grow and spread. Giving pembrolizumab after standard treatment with radiation plus chemotherapy may increase the ability of the immune system to fight LS-SCLC.

title: Mass photometry reveals stoichiometry and binding dynamics of bispecific tetravalent anti-VEGF-PD-1 antibody ivonescimab.
authors: Jajcanin Jozic N, Bishop J, O'Shea AR et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The bispecific antibody ivonescimab targets programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). Recent clinical trials have shown it has greater efficacy against PD-L1 positive non-small cell lung cancer than pembrolizumab (Keytruda), a frequently prescribed anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody. Ivonescimab binds to two VEGF and two PD-1 molecules, with complex formation through higher-order structure formation (or 'daisy chain' binding). However, the binding stoichiometries and interaction dynamics of ivonescimab with VEGF and PD-1 have not been characterized in depth.
METHODS: We used mass photometry (MP) and kinetic modeling to analyze these interactions, quantifying the complexes formed and their affinities. Dissociation constants (K D) for ivonescimab's binding to VEGF and PD-1 were calculated from equilibrium counts and real-time measurements, respectively.
RESULTS: VEGF drove oligomerization of ivonescimab, which bound VEGF predominantly in a 2:2 stoichiometry, with K D = 0.08 nM. Higher-order oligomeric complexes, present only at low abundance, displayed markedly weaker affinities (3.17 nM; 1.29 nM). Ternary complexes of ivonescimab with its two targets consistently presented two PD-1 antigens for each ivonescimab molecule, with a 1.66 nM K D for the binding of the first PD-1 and the slightly stronger 0.89 nM for the second PD-1 molecule.
CONCLUSIONS: MP confirmed VEGF-induced ivonescimab oligomerization and revealed that dimers, not higher-order structures, were the most stable stoichiometry. MP enables detailed analysis of antibody-antigen interactions, even for bispecific antibodies that interact with antigens with complex stoichiometries.

title: A retrospective study on neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio in the early treatment stage for stratifying the incidence of PD-1 inhibitor-related thyroid dysfunction.
authors: Liu J, Qin B, Li K et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) have been investigated in the context of immune-related adverse events, but whether they can stratify the incidence of PD-1 inhibitor-related thyroid dysfunction (irTD) remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between clinically accessible variables, including NLR and PLR at early-treatment stage, and the occurrence of irTD in patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and explored an incidence stratification approach based on routinely available parameters.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study was conducted at two hospitals and enrolled patients with advanced NSCLC who received PD-1 inhibitors between 1 February 2019 and 31 October 2022. NLR and PLR were measured at baseline, after one cycle and two cycles of PD-1 inhibitor administration. Analyses involving measurement after two cycles used a landmark analysis that excluded patients who had developed irTD before that measurement. Demographic characteristics, tumor- and treatment-related variables, history of thyroid disease, and baseline thyroid function were also collected. Univariable logistic regression, timepoint joint logistic regression models, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were used to evaluate the association between each candidate variable and irTD.
RESULTS: A total of 119 patients were included, of whom 20 experienced irTD (16.8%). Patients who developed irTD had lower NLR and PLR values at baseline, after one cycle, and after two cycles than those who did not. The AUC of NLR after one cycle was 0.830 (95% CI, 0.754-0.899); at baseline and after two cycles, the AUCs were 0.665 (95% CI, 0.520-0.793) and 0.722 (95% CI, 0.596-0.849), respectively. When NLR values from two timepoints were entered simultaneously into the model, NLR after one cycle remained associated with irTD (OR 0.148, 95% CI, 0.052-0.422; P < 0.001). The incidence of irTD was 30.0% (15/50) in patients younger than 65 years and 7.2% (5/69) in those aged 65 years or older. After stratification by NLR after one cycle < 2.43 and age < 65 years, the incidence rates in patients with 0, 1, and 2 risk factors were 0.0% (0/39), 9.8% (5/51), and 51.7% (15/29), respectively.
CONCLUSION: NLR measured after one cycle of PD-1 inhibitor and age were associated with the stratification of irTD incidence. This stratification might serve as a supplementary clue for thyroid function monitoring but could not replace it, and prospective external validation was required.

title: Advances in personalized management strategies for ground-glass opacity-featured lung cancer.
authors: Li T, Zhang Y, Chen H
abstract: Low-dose computed tomography has increased the detection of ground-glass opacity (GGO)-featured lung cancer. Evidence from radiologic-pathologic correlation, molecular profiling, and clinical outcome studies indicates that GGO-featured lung cancer is both a distinct clinical phenotype and a special stage in the evolution of lung adenocarcinoma. Its management differs from that of conventional solid lung cancer. As evidence accumulates for the surgical curative time window, selective mediastinal lymph node management, and active surveillance of multifocal GGO, the field is shifting from simple "early detection and early treatment" toward early precise intervention; from disease-centered treatment toward whole-course patient benefit; and from survival extension toward cure. The central strategy is to exclude benign or self-limited lesions, compare the lesion's natural course with the patient's life expectancy, and integrate nodule size, solid component, lesion location, frozen-section pathology, and expected pulmonary function loss to determine surveillance interval, surgical timing, and extent of resection. Under the concept of minimally invasive surgery 3.0, treatment should shift from maximally tolerated intervention to minimum effective treatment. This expert review summarizes recent advances in personalized management of GGO-featured lung cancer and discusses how surveillance, parenchyma-sparing surgery, selective lymph node management, and postoperative follow-up can be tailored to pursue cure while avoiding overtreatment.

title: Pulmonary Carcinosarcoma in a Never-Smoker: An Unusually Prolonged Prediagnostic Course.
authors: Zuniga-Kwon H, Torres L, Talledo O et al.
abstract: Pulmonary carcinosarcoma is a rare biphasic malignancy accounting for < 1% of lung cancers, typically affecting older male smokers and often diagnosed beyond a localised stage. We report a 71-year-old never-smoker whose lesion was initially interpreted as community-acquired pneumonia. Despite resolution of symptoms and inflammatory changes with antibiotics, the lesion persisted and enlarged. PET/CT showed FDG uptake (SUVmax 9.4) without metastatic disease, favouring residual inflammation. Retrospective review of imaging for unrelated indications demonstrated a lesion at the same anatomical site since 2019, with slow initial growth followed by acceleration after 2024. Robot-assisted wedge resection followed by completion lobectomy and lymph node dissection confirmed pulmonary carcinosarcoma (pT2aN0M0, Stage IB). The patient remained disease-free 8 months after surgery. This unusually prolonged, image-documented prediagnostic interval suggests that the radiological evolution of pulmonary carcinosarcoma may be more heterogeneous than published series indicate and underscores the value of reviewing prior imaging when evaluating a pulmonary lesion.

title: Development of a lung nodule volumetry tool for quality assurance assessment of low-dose lung cancer screening CT protocols.
authors: Siddiki Y, Gallego Manzano L, Pozzessere C et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-dose CT (LDCT) is the preferred modality for lung nodule detection and follow-up, yet standardized quality-control criteria are lacking. Volumetric accuracy is clinically important but strongly dependent on segmentation and reconstruction settings, particularly for small, low-contrast subsolid nodules, and frameworks for optimizing LDCT protocols based on volumetric performance remain limited.
PURPOSE: To develop a lung nodule segmentation and volumetry tool that evaluates volumetric accuracy across CT reconstruction settings and to demonstrate how accuracy and repeatability metrics can support protocol comparison as a quality-assurance assessment.
METHODS: A custom semi-automatic tool was developed in Python and evaluated using the QRM Thorax phantom on a GE Revolution Apex CT system. Fifteen artificial nodules were analyzed, combining five diameters (3-12 mm) and three attenuation levels (100, -630, -800 HU). Reconstruction parameters were systematically varied, including kernel (STANDARD, LUNG), slice thickness (0.625-2.5 mm), spacing (0.625, 1.25 mm), algorithm (DLIR-H and ASiR-V at 80%), and field of view (18, 36 cm). Performance was assessed using mean relative volume error (target within ± 20%), repeatability coefficient (RC), and size-specific RMSE; the best-performing configuration per nodule type served as reference. Reconstruction effects were evaluated using factorial ANOVA, Levene's test, Welch's t-test, and bootstrap analysis with false-discovery-rate correction.
RESULTS: Overall mean relative volume errors ranged from -7.1% to 6.7% for solid nodules and -14.7% to 5.8% for type 1 subsolid nodules ≥ 5 mm; type 2 subsolid nodules showed larger deviations (-27.1% to -12.1%). Nodule size and reconstruction kernel were the dominant contributors to mean volume error, while slice thickness and spacing mainly influenced variability. Significant differences from the reference were found for four solid-nodule settings, none for type 1, and one for type 2 subsolid settings, with degradation occurring mainly at increased slice thickness or reduced field of view. The 3 mm subsolid nodules showed consistently high variability across all settings.
CONCLUSIONS: The tool enabled quantitative comparison of CT reconstruction settings using volumetric accuracy and repeatability metrics. For clinically relevant sizes ( ≥ 5 mm), volumetric performance remained within the predefined technical-suitability range across most settings, supporting use of the tool for protocol evaluation and future dose-optimization studies.

title: Compartmental immune responses and biomarker discordance after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Han S, Ma Y, Li Z et al.
abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy can produce uneven responses across the primary tumour, regional lymph nodes, and occult systemic disease. Pathology, circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), and imaging capture different consequences of this response, so their disagreement can contain clinically relevant biological information. This structured narrative review examines same-patient evidence in resectable non-small cell lung cancer and interprets discordance through anatomical compartment, sampling time, and local immune context. Paired tissue studies show distinct primary and nodal immune ecologies and response-associated lymphoid and myeloid programmes. Spatial clonality and unequal shedding shape the circulating signal, while inflammatory and reparative tissue changes can sustain imaging abnormalities after tumour regression. These observations inform four proposed principles for multidisciplinary interpretation. Separate primary and nodal reporting preserves compartment-specific response information. Presurgical ctDNA clearance indicates molecular response, not proof of tissue eradication. Confirmed postoperative molecular conversion provides a rationale for reassessing current disease status. For imaging conflicts that could alter curative-intent management, lesion-level review can identify when tissue confirmation would be feasible and decision-changing. A postoperative pathology-molecular residual disease matrix organises research questions while preserving nodal findings, unresolved lesions, and serial molecular trajectory. The immediate contribution is to identify which additional observation can resolve a consequential conflict; treatment adaptation then requires evidence that acting on the result benefits patients. Biomarker discordance is therefore an interpretive problem with biological content, rather than a reason to let the most favourable test define the entire response.

title: Validation of Interstitial Lung Disease Coding in US Claims Data in Patients with Solid Tumors.
authors: Shen M, Wang S, Schneeweiss S et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: The validity of ILD coding in US claims data among patients with cancer remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a study to test the validity of ILD coding in claims data in patients with lung, breast, ovarian, endometrial, cervical, or colorectal cancer. We used electronic health record (EHR) data from the Mass General Brigham Health Care System linked with Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial claims data from 01/01/2017 to 12/31/2024. The base algorithm required two ICD-10-CM codes for ILD, each 7 to 180 days apart. Several nested algorithms additionally requiring ILD coding by a pulmonologist, ILD-relevant procedure, excluding autoimmune diseases, and requiring chemo/immunotherapy treatment were defined. The positive predictive values (PPVs) of each claims-based algorithm were calculated against the reference standard established through chart review by pulmonologists.
RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 360 patients. PPV of the base algorithm was 59% (95% confidence interval: 53%-64%). The algorithm additionally requiring ILD-relevant procedure with chemo- or immunotherapy administration and excluding those with autoimmune conditions was 64% (57%-71%). The PPV of base algorithm among patients with colorectal cancer was the lowest - 38% (24%-52%). The PPVs improved meaningfully when the index diagnosis of ILD was coded by a pulmonologist, ranging from 78-88% across different algorithms.
CONCLUSION: We found that, in patients diagnosed with lung, breast, gynecologic, or colorectal cancer, claims-based ILD diagnoses demonstrated moderate to low alignment with a reference standard by expert chart review. It can be improved when ILD is coded by a pulmonologist, though at the cost of substantially fewer cases of ILD identified.

title: Multi-omics profiling identifies a CXCL9-PD-1+ CD8+ T cell axis for prediction of checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis.
authors: Bi N, Jiang Z, Yang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a life-threatening complication of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). We aimed to identify predictive biomarkers associated with symptomatic CIP (sCIP) and unravel the underlying pathogenesis.
METHODS: We integrated CyTOF, proteomics, single-cell RNA and V(D)J sequencing, single-cell secretomics, and spatial transcriptomics. These techniques were used to profile peripheral blood, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and lung tissue samples from two prospective multi-center cohorts of NSCLC patients receiving ICI combination treatments.
RESULTS: Elevated serum CXCL9 levels combined with high frequencies of peripheral PD-1+ CD8+ T cells after induction ICI were associated with subsequent sCIP (AUC=0.954) and inferior overall survival (HR=7.19, p=0.004). Mechanistically, PD-1+ CD8+ T cells displayed a type 1 effector profile characterized by IFN-γ and MIP-1β secretion. CXCL9/CXCR3 signaling was associated with recruitment of these cells to inflamed lung tissue.
CONCLUSIONS: The CXCL9-PD-1+ CD8+ T cell axis is associated with CIP pathogenesis. This mechanism supports a potential blood-based biomarker model for CIP risk stratification and identifies a promising preventive therapeutic target to optimize clinical management.

title: Machine learning classification of respiratory diseases using integrated breath measurements from the Inflammacheck® Device.
authors: D'Cruz LG, Fox L, Chauhan M et al.
abstract: Background:Lung cancer and pneumonia can present with non-specific symptoms that overlap with other respiratory conditions. This study evaluated whether breath measurements from the Inflammacheck® device contain sufficient diagnostic information to support machine-learning classification of lung cancer and pneumonia.Methods:A secondary analysis of 282 participants with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, interstitial lung disease, bronchiectasis, breathing pattern disorder, pneumonia, lung cancer and healthy controls was undertaken. Seven device-derived variables comprising H₂O₂, exhalation duration, sample collection time and up to 6-minutes of tidal-breathing based peak CO₂, breath humidity, breath temperature, exhalation flow rate were analysed. Eight-class and three-class shrinkage linear discriminant analysis (LDA) models were evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation with out-of-fold predictions. Class-specific probability thresholds were scanned within prespecified 85-95% specificity ranges. An exploratory soft-voting ensemble combining LDA, Extra Trees, radial-basis-function support-vector machine and XGBoost was also evaluated.Results:Eight-class classification showed limited discrimination, whereas consolidation into three classes (lung cancer, pneumonia and other respiratory disease) improved diagnostic separation. At operating thresholds corresponding to approximately 89-90% specificity, the 3-class LDA demonstrated discriminatory ability for both lung cancer and pneumonia, with AUROCs of 0.650 and 0.728, respectively. The soft-voting ensemble model further improved discrimination, increasing AUROC to 0.725 for lung cancer and 0.753 for pneumonia.Conclusions:Inflammacheck® variables contain promising measurable discriminatory information for further development of a screening-tool. Future modelling of the underlying continuous breath time-series ("breathprint") using deep-learning approaches may extract additional discriminatory features not captured by participant-level summary measures.&#xD.

title: Survival Outcomes of Sequential Therapies in Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma: A Real-World Analysis of Second-Line Treatment With Nivolumab or Carboplatin-Pemetrexed.
authors: Maffezzoli M, Lau J, Dungey M et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Optimal treatment sequencing in malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) remains uncertain, particularly after progression on first-line (1L) treatment. We assessed real-world outcomes of patients receiving second-line (2L) carboplatin-pemetrexed (CARBO-PEM) after nivolumab-ipilimumab (NIVO-IPI), or 2L nivolumab (NIVO) after CARBO-PEM and explored the prognostic value of the Mesothelioma Risk Score (MRS) in the 1L setting.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included patients with advanced MPM treated across five UK institutions between May 2015 and November 2025. Eligible patients received either 2L CARBO-PEM after NIVO-IPI, or 1L CARBO-PEM followed by 2L NIVO. The primary end point was overall survival (OS) from 1L treatment initiation.
RESULTS: Overall, 147 patients were included, and 54 received NIVO-IPI followed by CARBO-PEM and 93 received CARBO-PEM followed by NIVO. The median age was 73.8 years and 83.0% had epithelioid histology. The median follow-up was 43.3 months from 1L initiation. The median OS was 23.55 months with CARBO-PEM followed by NIVO versus 25.53 months with NIVO-IPI followed by CARBO-PEM (hazard ratio 1.28 [95% CI, 0.82 to 2.01]; P = .270). The median PFS 2L was 3.65 months with 2L NIVO versus 6.15 months with 2L CARBO-PEM, without statistical significance, while median OS 2L was 12.53 months and 14.11, respectively. In the 1L setting, MRS showed limited discrimination for PFS and OS. Grade ≥2 irAEs during NIVO-IPI were associated with longer PFS 1L but not OS.
CONCLUSION: In patients with MPM receiving 2L therapy, CARBO-PEM after NIVO-IPI remains clinically active, and OS appeared similar across treatment sequences. These findings support sequence flexibility in fit patients but highlight the need for more robust prognostic biomarkers.

title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma.
authors: Arnould M, Assie JB, Meiller C et al.
abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

title: Comparison of Single-Port and Two-Port Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery for Thymoma Resection.
authors: Yang Z, Yu L, Ruan H et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the clinical efficacy and safety of single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (SP-VATS) versus two-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (TP-VATS) in patients undergoing thymoma resection.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data from 162 consecutive patients who underwent VATS thymoma resection at the Department of Thoracic Surgery, Beijing Chest Hospital, between August 2009 and March 2024. Patients were categorized according to the surgical approach into the TP-VATS group (n = 115) and the SP-VATS group (n = 47). Baseline clinical characteristics, perioperative safety outcomes, and surgical efficacy were systematically compared between the two groups. In addition, potential factors contributing to intraoperative conversion to thoracotomy were evaluated.
RESULTS: All patients successfully completed the planned surgical procedures and were discharged without perioperative mortality. In the TP-VATS group, one patient required intraoperative conversion to thoracotomy. Compared with the TP-VATS group, patients in the SP-VATS group experienced a significantly shorter operative time (median: 110 vs. 80 min, P = 0.013), lower intraoperative blood loss (median: 50 vs. 20 mL, P < 0.001), and a shorter postoperative hospital stay (median: 8 vs. 7 days, P = 0.029). Multiple linear regression analysis demonstrated that, in the clinical baseline model evaluating operative time (Model 1), SP-VATS was independently associated with a reduced operative duration, with unstandardized coefficient (B) of 19.99 (95% CI: 0.87-39.11, P = 0.041). Consistently, in the preoperative clinical assessment model (Model 2), SP-VATS remained significantly associated with operative time reduction B = 19.00, 95% CI: -0.44-38.45, P = 0.045).
CONCLUSION: Multiple linear regression modeling indicates that the choice of surgical approach influences perioperative risk profiles in patients undergoing thymectomy for thymoma. Compared with TP-VATS, SP-VATS was associated with a statistically significant but clinically modest reduction in operative time and estimated blood loss, while maintaining procedural safety. These findings suggest that SP-VATS represents an effective and favorable surgical option that thoracic surgeons may consider for thymoma resection; however, the clinical relevance of the observed reductions should be interpreted with caution. Further studies incorporating patient-centered outcomes and cost-effectiveness analyses are needed to determine the clinical importance of these perioperative differences.

title: Clinical Response to Lenvatinib in a Pediatric Case of Unresectable Chemotherapy-Refractory Thymic Carcinoma.
authors: Kitamura S, Abematsu T, Horikawa S et al.

title: Quality benchmarks in CRS-HIPEC surgery: An 11-year single-center analysis of outcomes, safety, and perioperative performance (2014-2024).
authors: Kazanowski M, Lesiak P, Wierzbicki J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quality indicators (QIs) are central to safe delivery of cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC), yet program-level benchmarking across tumor types is scarce.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the structure, process, and outcome QIs of a single-center CRS-HIPEC program (2014-2024) and to assess temporal trends in cytoreduction completeness, early mortality, length of stay (LOS), renal safety, and multidisciplinary team (MDT) integration against contemporary international benchmarks.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of consecutive CRS-HIPEC procedures (2014-2024) was conducted at a Polish tertiary center. Prespecified QIs included complete or near-complete cytoreduction (CC-0/1), 30- and 90-day mortality, LOS, LOS > 10 days, unplanned reoperation, 30-day readmission, MDT uptake, and acute kidney injury (AKI; defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) serum creatinine criteria). Time trends were displayed with Shewhart charts and funnel plots; Wilson's 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were used for proportions.
RESULTS: Among 319 procedures (colorectal cancer (CRC) 111; ovarian cancer 87; mesothelioma/other 57; low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm/pseudomyxoma peritonei (LAMN/PMP) 52; gastric cancer 12), the CC-0/1 rate was 93.4% overall (CRC 96.4%; LAMN/PMP 100%; ovarian cancer 90.8%; gastric cancer 91.7%; mesothelioma/other 86.0%). Thirtyand 90-day mortality were 0.6% and 1.6%, respectively; tumor-specific 30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 1.9%. Median LOS fell from 8.6 to 7.4 days (2014-2018 vs 2019-2024), and LOS > 10 days declined from 25.0% to 13.2%. Peritoneal cancer index (PCI) correlated weakly with LOS (Spearman's ρ = 0.13, p = 0.019), while AKI occurred in 70/308 (22.7%, 95% CI: 18.4-27.7), predominantly stage 1; AKI did not differ by cisplatin exposure (26.0% vs 21.2%, p = 0.389). The proportion of procedures with documented MDT discussion increased to approx. 20-33% after 2018.
CONCLUSIONS: Over 11 years, a single-center CRS-HIPEC program achieved high-quality cytoreduction with low early mortality and a reduction in LOS, meeting or exceeding contemporary QI standards. Incorporating AKI and MDT uptake into routine audit supports comprehensive, program-level benchmarking.

title: Lipofibroadenoma of the Thymus: A Case Report With Literature Review and Differential Diagnostic Considerations.
authors: Ntalakos N, Arnaouti M, Chlapoutakis S et al.
abstract: Thymic lipofibroadenoma is a rare lesion composed of mature adipose tissue, fibrous stroma, and thymic epithelial elements. We describe a 51-year-old woman with recurrent syncope and a large anterior mediastinal mass compressing adjacent cardiac structures. Complete excision yielded an encapsulated, multilobulated mass measuring 14 × 4 × 2 cm. Histology showed bland epithelial strands and cords within dense hyalinized stroma admixed with mature fat and Hassall corpuscles. Epithelial cells expressed cytokeratins AE1/AE3 and 19, supporting the diagnosis of lipofibroadenoma. At six months, the patient was asymptomatic without imaging evidence of recurrence. A narrative review of 18 previously published cases addresses the clinicopathologic spectrum and differential diagnosis, particularly the overlap with thymolipoma and thymofibrolipoma. Reported outcomes generally favor benign behavior, although limited and uneven follow-up prevents firm conclusions about long-term recurrence risk.

title: Gene regulatory logic underlying the differentiation of mixed lineages in human thymic epithelial cells.
authors: Prabakar RK, Chapin SR, Lin Y et al.
abstract: The thymus enacts central tolerance through thymic epithelial cells (TECs), which present self-antigens to developing T cells to remove self-reactive cells, preventing autoimmunity. Human TECs include populations that express lineage-committed programs corresponding to distinct peripheral tissues, yet how they acquire these programs and whether these TEC subpopulations are genetically related and conserved in mice remain unknown. Using matched single-cell gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility profiling of 126,687 human TECs, we identified 17 TEC subsets defined by their distinct expression profiles of 1,843 cell type restricted-antigens (CRAs) from 48 peripheral cell types. With a new phylogenetic reconstruction method, we show that lineage-committed TECs share a common ancestor, retain a thymus-specific mixed identity through co-expression of multiple CRA signatures, and are specified by coordinated activator and repressor regulons. We also identified a basement-membrane-collagen-rich state (BMC-TECs) with progenitor-like properties. Finally, mouse TECs shared the regulatory strategy but conserved few master transcription-factor drivers. This study mechanistically characterizes human TEC subpopulations and reveals the gene regulatory logic that leads to their distinct diversification and mixed identities in humans and mice.

title: Epigenomic circuits shaping cellular heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma.
authors: Giotti B, Chang L, Dolasia K et al.
abstract: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is an aggressive and lethal malignancy with current treatments offering limited clinical benefit. In this study, we utilized single-cell chromatin accessibility and transcriptomic profiling of patient-matched samples to infer the epigenomic regulation underlying cellular heterogeneity in PM. High-resolution epigenomic profiling suggested transcriptional regulators with putative pro-tumoral roles in mesothelioma, whose function was experimentally tested using genetic perturbations across four PM cell lines. Furthermore, we observed several putative associations between epigenomic circuits and macrophage ontogeny, a sarcomatoid-like neoplastic state, and a fetal-like endothelial cell state. Our analysis also showed similarities between the chromatin accessibility landscapes of exhausted CD8 T and KLRC1 natural killer cells and identified NR4A2 as a potential shared regulator of dysfunction in both lymphocyte subsets. We further identified a state-specific distal enhancer near NR4A2 and experimentally validated its regulation of NR4A2 expression in Jurkat cells. Together, we provide an epigenomic map of PM and nominate candidate transcription factors and regulatory elements for future functional investigation, including their potential relevance to epigenetic editing strategies to limit tumor growth and enhance anti-tumor immunity.

title: Real-world outcomes of second-line therapy in advanced thymic carcinoma: a multicenter Turkish Oncology Group (TOG) study.
authors: Kus F, Atalah F, Sahin G et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thymic carcinoma (TC) is a rare and aggressive malignancy with limited evidence guiding second-line treatment after prior systemic therapy. We evaluated real-world outcomes of second-line systemic therapy in a multicenter cohort.
METHODS: Adults with unresectable, recurrent, or metastatic TC who received second-line systemic therapy after prior systemic therapy between 2010 and 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Treatments were categorized as multidrug chemotherapy, gemcitabine monotherapy, PD-1 inhibitor therapy, or targeted therapy (sunitinib). For the primary comparison of multidrug chemotherapy versus gemcitabine monotherapy, propensity scores based on age, sex, ECOG performance status, Masaoka-Koga stage IV, prior surgery, and calendar year were used to generate overlap weights. Weighted Cox models used robust standard errors clustered by treatment center. A sensitivity propensity-score model additionally included first-line carboplatin-paclitaxel exposure (yes/no).
RESULTS: A total of 107 patients from 20 treatment centers were included. Median age was 53.2 years (IQR, 41.5-58.0), 78 (72.9%) were male, 81 of 106 patients with available data (76.4%) had ECOG 0-1, and 61 (57.0%) had Masaoka-Koga stage IV disease at diagnosis. At a median follow-up of 35 months, median PFS and OS for the overall cohort were 13.6 and 35.0 months, respectively. In the primary overlap-weighted comparison (n = 89), multidrug chemotherapy was associated with a lower hazard of progression or death than gemcitabine monotherapy (HR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.14-0.59; p < 0.001) and a lower hazard of death (HR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.18-0.97; p = 0.043). In a sensitivity model additionally incorporating first-line carboplatin-paclitaxel exposure, the PFS estimate remained significant (HR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.16-0.65; p = 0.0015), whereas the OS estimate remained directionally similar but was less precise (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.19-1.11; p = 0.083). The PD-1 inhibitor group (n = 13) had median PFS and OS of 15.0 and 48.0 months, respectively, in unadjusted descriptive analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, multidrug chemotherapy was associated with lower hazards of progression or death and of death than gemcitabine monotherapy in the primary overlap-weighted analysis. A sensitivity analysis additionally accounting for first-line carboplatin-paclitaxel exposure preserved the PFS association and yielded a similar but less precise OS estimate. Outcomes observed with PD-1 inhibitors were favorable but should be interpreted descriptively because of the small sample size, later treatment era, and potential residual confounding. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

title: The role of imaging studies in the diagnosis of thymic epithelial tumors: A radiologic-pathologic correlation.
authors: Stowell JT, Suster DI
abstract: Primary thymic epithelial neoplasms represent a rare family of tumors that include various neoplasms including thymoma, thymic carcinoma, thymic neuroendocrine tumors, and various benign epithelial tumors such as epithelial cysts. Imaging plays an important role in the initial diagnosis and management of thymic epithelial neoplasms and many of these tumors come to clinical attention during routine imaging studies performed for other reasons. Imaging features of thymoma and thymic carcinoma are variable and may often overlap among these entities, making differentiation of the World Health Organization histological subtypes difficult by imaging. A combination of chest radiography, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and nuclear medicine studies may be necessary for complete characterization and staging of lesions, especially in distinguishing other thymic conditions (thymic hyperplasia) from thymic malignancies and in staging the latter.

title: Bridging the molecular and immune landscapes of pleural mesothelioma: Implications for immune checkpoint inhibitor response.
authors: Soares-Gonçalves J, Carvalheiro C, Batista A et al.
abstract: Pleural mesothelioma is a rare, asbestos-related malignancy with limited therapeutic options and dismal survival. Despite regulatory efforts, ongoing exposures, long disease latency and cases without recognized exposure suggest that pleural mesothelioma will remain a global challenge for decades. Immune checkpoint inhibitors yield modest, although clinically meaningful benefit in a subset of patients, and histology alone incompletely captures the pronounced intra- and inter-patient heterogeneity that drives prognosis and treatment responses. Multi-omic studies depict pleural mesothelioma as a tumor suppressor loss malignancy with low mutation rates, extensive structural genomic damage and a spectrum of immune states. In this review, we bridge genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic and immune-profiling data to explain how asbestos-induced genomic fragility, germline predisposition and the tumor immune microenvironment interact to shape disease biology and therapeutic vulnerability. We highlight how histo-molecular and immune-vascular continua refine risk stratification beyond histology, and how recurrent alterations intersect with immune infiltration, checkpoint expression and T cell dysfunction to potentially modulate immune checkpoint inhibitors sensitivity. These insights support comprehensive and integrative profiling to develop robust biomarkers, optimize patient selection and guide rational combinatorial strategies.
